primary_claim: Trained OCEAN (Big-5) trait LoRAs, instilled via a modified Open Character Training pipeline across Llama-3.1/Qwen3/Gemma3 (4B-32B), reliably shift their target personality trait's self-identification and expression with minimal capability cost, can be scaled, inverted, and combined via simple weight-space arithmetic to amplify/suppress/compose traits, and moving along specific trait axes (e.g. reducing neuroticism, combining agreeableness and conscientiousness) measurably mitigates known LLM pathologies such as Gemma's frustration spirals and the jailbreak/overrefusal tradeoff.

effect.metric: LLM-judge trait expression shift and downstream pathology metrics
effect.value: all 10 OCEAN amplifier/suppressor LoRAs shift their own trait more than other traits with little/no capability cost on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; combining agreeableness+conscientiousness amplifiers reduces WildJailbreak harmful compliance rate while keeping benign-prompt overrefusal low, better than either trait alone; neuroticism suppression reduces Gemma-3-27B-IT frustration in the 'Gemma needs help' multi-turn setup; reducing agreeableness increases CoCoNot harmful compliance rate

depends_on: LessWrong: Gemma needs help (Soligo et al.)
contradicts_or_qualifies: Reproduces and extends Soligo et al.'s 'Gemma needs help' finding that Gemma-3-27B-IT becomes frustrated on impossible problems, showing neuroticism-suppressor LoRAs (and their sign-inverted amplifier counterparts) can mitigate this
stated_future_work: Better unsupervised trait discovery, ideally on real deployment trajectories across a range of models
Scale to much larger models, where the capability-cost tradeoff appears to become more favorable, not less
Map trait-space to downstream safety behaviours more systematically and search it for optimal personas
Extend rollouts beyond 15 turns to test long-term stability of trait modulations, e.g. for AI psychosis
Add more supervised traits (6/10/50) beyond the 5D OCEAN space
Test whether LoRA persona modifications generalize across different system-prompted situations or to models fine-tuned to a different base persona
limitations_stated: The TRAIT MCQ benchmark may not apply cleanly to an AI assistant, may not reflect coherent self-identification, and models may not answer honestly about their own traits
The full MCQ + LLM-judge evaluation stack was only run on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; other models/teachers were only evaluated on TRAIT and MMLU

The OCEAN LoRA adapters are not fully independent -- they shift traits other than their target, and even the 'neutral' control model (trained with a no-variation constitution) measurably shifts behavior, e.g. sycophantic apology rate
The historical-model (TimeCapsuleLM) robustness check produced mixed results: coherence was worse than on modern models and trait shift didn't generalise to all adapters
quote: The trained OCEAN LoRAs from our pipeline work. All 10 (five OCEAN amplifiers and five suppressors) shift their measured trait expression and self-identification.
